ShortDescription.Value: A better vanilla building menu: sorting, categories, filters and more details.

Publish.LongDescription:
A better version of the vanilla building menu, with sorting, categories and more details. Click any toolbar menu (Roads, Electricity, Education, Zones and the rest) and you get a panel instead of the row of icons.
* Grid, list, cards or table. Category tabs and a search box. * Sort by cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot, level or parking. * Group by type, theme, source, density, footprint, cost or progression. * Filter by unlocked, DLC, theme, asset pack, placement, role or source. Density has its own tabs. * Set a range for cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot width or lot depth. * Hover an asset to see its numbers and what unlocks it. * Building upgrades get names, cost and footprint too.
The list holds what the menu holds. Trees are under Landscaping; props, decals and hidden assets are not, and there is no object picker. Use Find It for those.
Works with Find It and does not replace it. Find It is a window over every asset in the game; this mod changes the toolbar menus. When Find It's window is open it takes the menu slot; this panel returns when it closes.
No Harmony patches, nothing saved to your city. Remove it any time.
**Options** (Options > Better Building Menu): switch back to the stock icon row; tile size; widen searches to every menu automatically.
Bugs and requests: the comments on this page.
Forked from Find It 1.5.8 by T. D. W. Thanks also to YenYang (UI), Algernon, Chameleon (icons) and Baka-gourd (focus handling).
This mod was developed with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude), under human direction and review.
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.3.0
Changes * The build menu opens where the game's own does, at its size. Pick one of five Widths in Options › Better Building Menu, or drag either side edge to one; every menu opens at it. At the wider Widths the tool options move left for room. * If you used an earlier version, the menu opens at the width nearest yours and Default view starts at your View. * The top edge settles on whole lines; dragged below the fewest lines it collapses the menu to search and tabs until a tab, typing or a double-click, which also restores the game's size. Options › Top edge: Whole lines, or Free, where you let go with no collapse; earlier versions' players start at Free. * The search, Sort, Filter, Group, View and close sit along the top edge; each opens a list a click elsewhere closes. View also offers Look, Width and More options…. * The search box names the building Enter places, or says All matches locked. Enter in the search arms the best match, wherever it sits, however sorted. * Control pane is now an option, off for new players, else as you had it. The pane's Reset menu is gone; Reset the build menu… in Options asks, then puts options, size and each menu's View and Group back. * Pick the chosen sort again to reverse it. In Group, Category is now By tab, None No groups. * With a terraforming brush the menu stays open and answers search and filters, as the game's does. * A sort's first click puts the best first (most capacity, lowest Cost or Upkeep), ties to the cheaper building. Sort by Households, Water capacity or Sewage capacity. * With Replace the vanilla build menu off, the other options grey out and say why. * With a controller the game's own build menu shows; move the mouse and this one returns on the same menu. * The tabs run along the bottom edge, by the toolbar: All with the menu's icon, then each tab's icon over a count following filters and search; an emptied tab keeps its place. Education's school levels are named chips beside its tab. * At the tabs' right end: the tab you are on; a value most buildings share, said once with its symbol where it fits (100 km/h unless shown), so only the others show theirs; and how many of the matches the list holds. The list ends in the button that loads more. * A menu opens on the tab you last picked a building from, that building on top, else its first tab (Education: first level); in Cards or with few buildings, on All. Opening a menu clears the search. * A sort, or a click on the lit tab, takes the list to its top; so does returning to that building's tab. * While typing, Up and Down change the building Enter places, marked ↵ in the list, and Page Up and Down scroll it; Esc closes an open list, clears the search, then closes the menu. * After Enter, a pick or closing the menu, the arrow keys move the camera again; the search box is outlined while typing. * On a wider menu each tab names itself beside its icon where all fit. A mark under the menu points to its toolbar button. * Options › Look draws every menu and the upgrades panel as Standard or Plates (units written out: 80 km/h); both follow the game's Interface style and transparency. * Each menu keeps its View (List, Icons, Tiles or Cards) and Group, and its Sort until you quit; Options › Default view, Auto at first, sets the rest: lists for most menus, icons for Landscaping and Signature Buildings, tiles for zones. Grid is now Tiles, Table List. * List gives each building a plate, 20 a screen, more when wider: its picture; its name, cut once with … keeping what tells it apart; its cost, a road's per cell (¢44/c); by a symbol its speed, capacity, workers or lot. Above 100% text, Options › At large text picks More buildings or Whole names. * Tiles shows pictures with their cost, tags look-alikes with what tells them apart and, in Standard, names the one pointed at; Options › Tile size is set to 64 once, then stays as you pick. A tile's tag shows a long cost in thousands or millions; under a number sort, that number. * Icons shows pictures alone, 45 a screen, more when wider; a family (Boulder 01–08) shows each number and shares a shade. * Point at a building for its card; Options › Hover card moves it to the game's detail slot or a line at the tabs' end. * Each View says MS n while the city waits on that milestone, else Locked (Icons where it fits), and keeps the unique and built marks. * Typing searches the whole menu, best first, Sort reading Match; clearing it brings back your tab and sort. * Cards are earlier versions' cards, three rows to the menu's height, each as wide as its name. * In All, each View names each tab with its count; a tab mostly locked lists what you can build first, then Locked, folded by a click. * A menu with few buildings shows them bigger in the list. At a wider Width, search results fill the columns under the search box first.
Fixed * A list that stops at 2,000 buildings says so, and how to narrow it. * Under Metric filters, a min or max that is not a number is outlined in red.
